feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: Jurors deliberate in the trial of rap icon Tupac Shakur's killing
entry.summary: Attorneys on Monday gave their closing arguments in the trial of Tupac Shakur's killing. The rap star was gunned down in a gang-related drive-by shooting in Las Vegas in 1996.

entry.title: Paperwork, lines, hours on hold: There's a 'Time Tax' on Americans who need help most
entry.summary: Annie Lowrey explores the administrative burdens people face applying for government benefits. It's not just about wasted time: "When the government treats us like this, we don't trust it," she says.

entry.title: At least 15 people missing after Grand Canyon flash flood
entry.summary: Several people are missing or unaccounted for after severe flash flooding in the Grand Canyon on Saturday caused significant damage.

entry.title: The U.S.-Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
entry.summary: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

entry.title: Rep. Glenn Ivey weighs stopgap spending bill as House returns to Washington
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Democratic Rep. Glenn Ivey of Maryland, as the House reconvenes this week with a stopgap spending bill on the agenda.

entry.title: Pentagon explores partially restoring civilian protection program
entry.summary: After internal pushback amongst top military officials over gutting a civilian protection program, the Pentagon is looking at partially restoring it.

entry.title: Arizona's taps won't run dry, but water bills will go up under federal plan for Colorado River
entry.summary: New federal rules mean Arizona will be getting a lot less water from the Colorado river. City leaders say they've been planning for years and no one will run out, but keeping taps flowing is expensive.

entry.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Telescope begins its journey into deep space
entry.summary: NASA launched a telescope named after Nancy Grace Roman, the pioneering astronomer whose work helped make Hubble and generations of space telescopes possible.

entry.title: Finally, an economic indicator you can eat
entry.summary: A corn dog may look like lunch. But to an economist, the price is a bigger story about food prices and inflation.

entry.title: Insanity defenses rarely work. Lindsay Clancy's case may be different
entry.summary: Insanity defenses are notoriously difficult to win. But Massachusetts law could give Lindsay Clancy a better chance.
